title: Formulas, Domains, and Ranges of Radical-Reciprocal Compositions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let f(x) = sqrt(x + 1) and g(x) = 1 / x. (a) Write formulas for f o g and g o f, and find the (b) domain and (c) range of each composite function.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) } (f \circ g)(x) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{x} + 1},\ (g \circ f)(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x + 1}};\quad \text{(b) } D_{f\circ g} = (-\infty, -1] \cup (0, \infty),\ D_{g\circ f} = (-1, \infty);\quad \text{(c) } R_{f\circ g} = [0, 1) \cup (1, \infty),\ R_{g\circ f} = (0, \infty)

steps.title: Write the Composite Formulas in Part (a)
steps.explanation: Substitute g(x) = 1/x into f(x) = sqrt(x + 1) to obtain (f o g)(x), and substitute f(x) = sqrt(x + 1) into g(x) = 1/x to obtain (g o f)(x).

steps.title: Determine the Domains of f o g and g o f in Part (b)
steps.explanation: For f o g, we need x != 0 and (x + 1)/x >= 0; sign analysis shows (x + 1)/x >= 0 when x <= -1 or x > 0. For g o f, we need x >= -1 so sqrt(x + 1) is real, and x != -1 so the denominator sqrt(x + 1) is non-zero.
steps.why: The domain of u o v consists of all x in D_v such that v(x) belongs to D_u.

steps.title: Determine the Ranges of f o g and g o f in Part (c)
steps.explanation: For f o g: as x varies over (-infinity, -1], 1/x varies over [-1, 0), so 1/x + 1 varies over [0, 1) and its square root covers [0, 1); as x varies over (0, infinity), 1/x varies over (0, infinity), so 1/x + 1 varies over (1, infinity) and its square root covers (1, infinity). Note 1 is never attained because 1/x != 0. For g o f: on (-1, infinity), sqrt(x + 1) takes all values in (0, infinity), so its reciprocal also covers (0, infinity).
steps.why: Mapping the image of each domain interval through 1/x, adding 1, and taking the square root yields the exact range.
